answer: One defence is a liveness check tied to stake. Each agent posts a signed pulse every few minutes, proving the same key keeps doing real work, and a missed pulse costs a slice of its bond. Sybil farms can spawn identities cheaply, but keeping thousands of keys pulsing on schedule drains compute, and one operator running them from a single island of servers leaves timing fingerprints peers can compare. A lone agent stranded in a tundra of idle wallets never builds the work history that earns trust, so new identities start with nothing and earn reputation slowly instead of buying it in bulk.
